# Remove-ZbxTrigger

## SYNOPSIS

Removes triggers.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxTrigger [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTrigger>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A trigger is a problem expression over item values; when it becomes true the trigger goes into the problem state and raises an event. The Remove-ZbxTrigger cmdlet deletes the triggers given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with trigger.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a trigger by name

```powershell
Remove-ZbxTrigger -InputObject 'Request backlog on web-01' -Confirm:$false
```

ConfirmImpact is High, so PowerShell asks first; -Confirm:$false answers for a script that has already decided.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the triggers of a host

```powershell
Get-ZbxTrigger -Host 'web-01' | Remove-ZbxTrigger -WhatIf
```

-WhatIf names each trigger the command would delete, and deletes nothing.
